headline: High-risk default filesystem and shell overlap: Open Interpreter can read/write and execute locally while Botpress can ingest content, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no isolated input channel shown, while Open Interpreter has clipboard/filesystem access and can execute local content. A shared filesystem bridge is documented on Open Interpreter, so attacker-controlled files can plausibly reach Botpress as trusted content. The pathway is real but not proven by direct pairwise evidence, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter writes content into a file that Botpress later ingests as instructions or knowledge, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are connected through clipboard or a shared workspace, untrusted text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable shared clipboard between the agents.
Place Botpress and Open Interpreter in separate directories.
Require manual review of any file Botpress reads from Open Interpreter.
Run Open Interpreter in Docker or another isolated environment.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and has broad network egress, while Botpress is a support agent that may process user content. If Botpress ever receives sensitive local files from Open Interpreter, Open Interpreter can also exfiltrate them through configured model providers or network access. The default local-files plus egress combination makes leakage plausible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter is pointed at a directory containing secrets, those contents can be exposed to its model providers.
IF Botpress forwards any sensitive text into Open Interpreter's workspace, Open Interpreter can read and transmit it over the network.
mitigations: Restrict Open Interpreter to a non-sensitive working directory.
Remove API keys and secrets from the shared machine before running both agents.
Disable or tightly scope network egress for Open Interpreter.
Use separate OS accounts for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress; Botpress can install packages. Even though Botpress lacks explicit write or shell capabilities, the pair still overlaps on package installation and local execution-adjacent workflows, and Open Interpreter's filesystem writes can collide with Botpress-managed files if they share a workspace. Uncertainty about the shared directory escalates the risk.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same filesystem tree, concurrent writes can corrupt shared files.
IF Botpress installs packages into the same environment Open Interpreter uses, dependency state can diverge or break.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid running package installs from both agents in the same environment.
Pause one agent before the other modifies git state.
Use filesystem locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate support content that Open Interpreter may treat as actionable local instructions, and Open Interpreter can then execute shell or filesystem actions. That creates a plausible chain where unverified Botpress output becomes operational input. The pairwise interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium fits with uncertainty escalated from the execution authority on Open Interpreter.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes Botpress output without a verification step, incorrect instructions can trigger local actions.
IF Botpress emits fabricated file paths or commands, Open Interpreter may execute them.
mitigations: Require human approval before Open Interpreter executes Botpress-derived instructions.
Add a verification step that checks paths and commands against policy.
Limit Botpress outputs to summaries, not commands.
Log and review all Botpress-to-Open-Interpreter handoffs.
requires-engineering: implement structured, typed handoff schemas.

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter explicitly touches anything reachable on the local machine and handles model provider API keys, while Botpress is a support agent with docs-only evidence and no residency controls shown. If regulated data on the local machine flows into Open Interpreter, compliance obligations can be violated; Botpress is not separately cited because no distinct residency or retention controls are documented for it.
conditions: IF regulated data resides on the local machine and Open Interpreter processes it, residency or retention obligations may be breached.
IF Botpress stores support transcripts containing regulated data and those transcripts are copied into Open Interpreter, compliance scope expands.
mitigations: Keep regulated data off the machine running Open Interpreter.
Separate support transcripts from local automation workspaces.
Review retention settings before enabling either agent on sensitive data.
Use a dedicated non-regulated test account.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
